newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close higher led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close higher led by blue chips.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday in thin trading led by a rise in blue chip shares traded on the Maof index, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.66 percent, or 1.59 points, to 243.93 on low all-share turnover of 80 million shekels against 72 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.85 percent higher at 252.47.

"The main reason for today's rise was hopes for the establishment of a unity government. With such a government the political situation will become more stable," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
The Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth reported on Tuesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to give his approval soon for a national unity government with the opposition Labour party.
Traders said Maof options speculators were active, exploiting the low volume to move prices.

"I believe that the trend is positive," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance. "The market lost almost 10 percent during the last correction and stocks are cheap. The earning reports published so far were above expectations and the outlook is positive."
"Share prices are very attractive and the only thing that prevents the market from rising is political uncertainty," Nahum said.
Bezeq Israel Telecom rose 0.75 percent to 859 agorot. The company said net profit in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose to 194.5 million shekels from 176 million shekels a year earlier.

Clal Industries lost 0.25 percent to 1,600 agorot. The holding company reported a net loss of 14.6 million shekels in the final quarter of 1996 as against net profit of 43 million shekels at the same period last year.
Electra Consumer closed unchanged at 1,776 agorot. Electra reported a fourth-quarter net loss of 7.4 million shekels as against net profit of 7.1 million a year earlier.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 1.0 percent to 542 agorot on volume of 5.2 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 3.25 percent to 652 agorot on turnover of 3.8 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.0 percent to 19,284 agorot on turnover of 3.6 million shekels.
